water.note: Avoid tap water; use bottled or filtered water even though some areas claim treated supply.

transit.pay: Most rail lines use the Beep contactless stored-value card, tappable at turnstiles and reloadable at stations; jeepneys and buses are still largely cash-only with fares paid to the driver or conductor.
transit.hours: Rail lines generally run about 4:30/5am to 10-11pm; no regular overnight service, so Grab or taxis are used late at night.
transit.note: Traffic congestion is severe, so rail (LRT/MRT) is often faster than road transport during peak hours despite crowding.

landmarks: Rizal Park (Luneta)
This vast historic park, site of national hero Jose Rizal's execution, is Manila's green civic heart and a classic sunset gathering spot.
Fort Santiago, Intramuros
The formidable Spanish-era citadel gate, with its iconic stone facade and moat, anchors the walled city and evokes centuries of colonial history.
Manila Cathedral
The grand baroque-revival cathedral in Intramuros, rebuilt multiple times after wars and quakes, is a majestic symbol of the city's Catholic heritage.
San Agustin Church
A UNESCO World Heritage Site and the oldest stone church in the Philippines, renowned for its trompe-l'oeil ceiling and ornate baroque facade.
Manila Bay Sunset
One of the world's most celebrated sunsets, painting the bay's skyline in fiery colors and drawing crowds along the Baywalk every evening.
Rizal Monument
The bronze and granite monument guarding the ashes of national hero Jose Rizal is a solemn, must-photograph centerpiece of Rizal Park.
Binondo (Manila Chinatown)
Established in 1594, the world's oldest Chinatown bursts with lantern-lined streets, temples, and legendary street food.
Quiapo Church
Home to the revered Black Nazarene statue, this bustling downtown church draws massive crowds and is a vivid slice of Filipino devotion and daily life.
National Museum of Fine Arts
Housed in the grand old Legislative Building, this neoclassical landmark showcases the Philippines' finest artworks including Juan Luna's Spoliarium.
SM Mall of Asia Eye
A giant illuminated Ferris wheel on the Manila Bay waterfront, one of the city's most photogenic modern landmarks especially at night.

train.note: The Philippines is an archipelago with no international rail. PNR's long-distance services have been suspended since 2024 while the North-South Commuter Railway is built, so there is effectively no intercity train from Manila - check the PNR site for the current position. The LRT and MRT lines are urban transit only. Travel between provinces is by bus, boat or plane.

bus.note: No international coaches - the Philippines has no land border. Manila has no single terminal: Cubao, Pasay and the PITX interchange in Parañaque each serve different regions, with Victory Liner (https://www.victoryliner.com/), Philtranco (https://philtranco.com.ph/) and Genesis running to Baguio (about 5 hours on the expressway), Legazpi and the Bicol region. Some southbound coaches continue onto ferries toward the Visayas. Book through the operators or Biyaheroes.

ferry.note: There are no international sailings from Manila. 2GO's overnight and multi-day inter-island ships leave from North Harbor and are a cheap, characterful alternative to flying - Cebu takes about 24 hours. Book ahead and expect delays and cancellations during the June-November typhoon season. The Corregidor boat is a day-trip service to the wartime island fortress in Manila Bay.
